Purpose: Detects whether input is text, user story, Figma link, Figma screenshot, or mixed; builds an input manifest with source IDs
Steps (PROPOSED): List each input: text, story, Figma link, screenshot. | Give each an ID: T-01, SS-01, FIG-01. | Write the input manifest with source for each.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every input has an ID and a source.

Purpose: Converts a request into 'As a… I want… so that…' stories with a source reference
Steps (PROPOSED): Read the request text. | Write each story as 'As a… I want… so that…'. | Cite the source ID on each story.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each story cites a source ID.

Purpose: Writes testable criteria, including iOS vs Android behavior
Steps (PROPOSED): For each story, write Given/When/Then criteria. | Add iOS vs Android behavior where the source gives it. | Mark unknown behavior TBD.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each criterion has one observable result.

Purpose: Lists ambiguities and missing details; each question offers options, none chosen by the agent
Steps (PROPOSED): List ambiguities and missing details. | Give at least two options per question. | Log each question; choose no answer.
Verification (PROPOSED): No question has an answer chosen by the agent.

Purpose: Verifies a story meets the team's Definition of Ready
Steps (PROPOSED): Check each story against the team's Definition of Ready. | Record pass or fail per item with evidence. | Send Ready to the Product Owner for approval.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every item has pass/fail evidence. The team's Definition of Ready text is TBD.

Purpose: Defines supported browsers, OS versions, devices, screen sizes or orientations
Steps (PROPOSED): Collect target platforms from the request. | List browser, OS, device, and screen scope. | Log each gap as TBD.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every platform has a version or TBD.

Purpose: Lists every screen and user flow from the input, with node or region IDs
Steps (PROPOSED): List every screen named in the input. | List the flows between screens. | Cite the node or region ID for each.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every screen has a source ID.

Purpose: Defines loading, empty, error, offline, permission-denied states; unknown states become open questions
Steps (PROPOSED): For each screen, check loading, empty, error, offline, and permission-denied. | Define the states the source gives. | Log any unknown state as an open question.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each screen has all five states or an open question.

Purpose: Writes screen-level UX spec; design choices the source does not make are left for a human decision
Steps (PROPOSED): Write a screen-level spec from the inventory and states. | Leave undecided choices for a human. | Cite the source for each item.
Verification (PROPOSED): No spec item lacks a source or an open question.

Purpose: Confirms every story maps to a screen or stated request; features an agent suggests go to Decision request, never into scope
Steps (PROPOSED): Map each story to a source. | Flag any story with no source. | Send agent suggestions to a decision request.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every story is mapped or flagged.

Purpose: From the user story text only: user journeys, screen list, navigation map, screen states. Labeled PROPOSED until a human approves
Steps (PROPOSED): Derive user journeys from the story text. | List screens and navigation between them. | Define screen states and label the output PROPOSED.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every screen traces to a story and carries the PROPOSED label.

Purpose: Text wireframe per screen: regions, primary action, components, order of content. Labeled PROPOSED
Steps (PROPOSED): Write a text wireframe per screen: regions, primary action, content order. | Label it PROPOSED with a reason.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each screen has exactly one primary action.

Purpose: Default colors, type scale, spacing, radius as proposed values, each with a reason. Replaced when a design source arrives
Steps (PROPOSED): Propose colors, type scale, spacing, and radius. | Give a reason for each value. | Label all values PROPOSED.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every value has a reason and a PROPOSED label. Contrast is checked with a tool (4.5:1 text).

Purpose: Checks the baseline and built UI against the minimum requirements (primary action, states, labels, touch targets, contrast, text scaling, feedback)
Steps (PROPOSED): Check: one primary action, states, labels, touch targets, contrast, text scaling, feedback. | Record pass or fail per item. | Use the target sizes the source sets; default sizes are PROPOSED.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every item is marked pass or fail with evidence.

Purpose: Writes component spec: props, states, variants, sizes
Steps (PROPOSED): List the components on each screen. | Write props, states, variants, and sizes for each.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each component lists its states.

Purpose: Defines layout for web breakpoints and mobile sizes, orientations, safe areas, text scaling
Steps (PROPOSED): Define a layout rule per breakpoint (web) and per mobile size and orientation. | Define safe areas and text scaling.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each screen has a rule for each supported size. Missing sizes are TBD.

Purpose: Creates tokens/theme file when none exists; adoption needs human approval
Steps (PROPOSED): Check whether a theme or token file exists. | Draft the token file. | Request human approval and do not adopt it.
Verification (PROPOSED): The file is marked not adopted until a named approval is recorded.

Purpose: Creates architecture decision records (context, options, decision, consequences)
Steps (PROPOSED): Write the context. | List at least two options. | Record the decision as proposed; a human records the final one with a date.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each ADR has at least two options and consequences.

Purpose: Compares candidate frameworks (web or mobile) against project needs and team skills
Steps (PROPOSED): List candidate frameworks for the platform. | Compare them to needs and team skills; TBD where data is missing. | Present the comparison to a human.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every comparison cell cites a source or says TBD.

Purpose: Defines layers, state management, module boundaries
Steps (PROPOSED): Define the layers. | Define the state approach and module boundaries. | Record the choice as an ADR.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each module has one owner.

Purpose: Writes OpenAPI or GraphQL contracts for backend calls
Steps (PROPOSED): List endpoints from the UX flows. | Write the OpenAPI or GraphQL contract. | Run the contract linter.
Verification (PROPOSED): The linter passes.

Purpose: Designs stack, tab, modal navigation and deep links from the UX flow inventory
Steps (PROPOSED): Map each screen to a stack, tab, or modal. | Define deep links.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every screen in the inventory appears once in the navigation map.

Purpose: Proposes folder and module layout for the app repo
Steps (PROPOSED): Propose folders and modules. | Check them against the team's seed template.
Verification (PROPOSED): The template check passes. Template location is TBD.

Purpose: Writes one consolidated design doc from ADRs, flows and contracts
Steps (PROPOSED): Collect the ADRs, flows, and contracts. | Write one document with a section for each. | Add an open-questions section.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each section cites an ADR, flow, or contract.

Purpose: Splits the approved design into Kanban-sized tasks linked to stories
Steps (PROPOSED): Split the design into tasks sized for one PR. | Link each task to its story ID.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every story maps to at least one task.

Purpose: Requests named human approval; never records approval itself
Steps (PROPOSED): Send the design document to the named approver. | Wait for the decision.
Verification (PROPOSED): Approval is recorded by a named person with a date. The agent never sets it.

Purpose: Writes screens, components, and business logic from a story and design
Steps (PROPOSED): Read the task and the approved design. | Write the screens, components, and logic. | Run the Task Gate.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each acceptance criterion has a code path.

Purpose: Applies the project's chosen state and navigation patterns consistently
Steps (PROPOSED): Use the state and navigation pattern from the ADR. | Apply it consistently across screens.
Verification (PROPOSED): Lint or review finds no mixed pattern.

Purpose: Creates branches, conventional commits, linked to kanban.md item IDs
Steps (PROPOSED): Create a branch named with the task ID. | Write conventional commit messages.
Verification (PROPOSED): Branch and commit names match the pattern.

Purpose: Writes PR descriptions with summary, test notes, screenshots, linked issues
Steps (PROPOSED): Write the summary, test notes, and linked task IDs. | Open the PR.
Verification (PROPOSED): CI is green before review starts.

Purpose: Maintains build tool settings (e.g. Gradle, Xcode, Vite/Webpack, Flutter/RN) and env variables
Steps (PROPOSED): Change build config only for the task. | Run the build.
Verification (PROPOSED): The build succeeds.

Purpose: Reproduces a reported bug, identifies root cause, applies a minimal fix
Steps (PROPOSED): Reproduce the bug from its steps. | Find the root cause. | Apply a minimal fix with a test.
Verification (PROPOSED): The test fails before the fix and passes after it.

Purpose: Writes a short plan per task (files, tests, risks) before coding
Steps (PROPOSED): List the files to change. | List tests and risks.
Verification (PROPOSED): The plan lists every file changed later.

Purpose: Generates components from an approved component spec (baseline or design-derived) using the design tokens
Steps (PROPOSED): Read the approved component spec and tokens. | Generate the component.
Verification (PROPOSED): No color or spacing value is hardcoded outside the tokens.

Purpose: Connects UI to the data/API layer as designed; adds no behavior beyond the story
Steps (PROPOSED): Connect the UI to the data layer as the contract says. | Add no behavior beyond the story.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each wired call matches the contract.

Purpose: Runs lint, type check and unit tests; commits only when all pass
Steps (PROPOSED): Run lint, type check, and unit tests. | Commit only if all three pass.
Verification (PROPOSED): All three results are recorded.

Purpose: Produces test plan per story or release covering scope, risks, environments
Steps (PROPOSED): List scope from the stories. | List risks and environments. | Name the test types for each story.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every acceptance criterion is in scope.

Purpose: Writes unit tests for the stack in use (e.g. Jest, pytest, flutter_test) for logic and state; Developer runs them in Task Gate
Steps (PROPOSED): Read the logic and state code. | Write tests for each branch.
Verification (PROPOSED): Tests pass in the Task Gate.

Purpose: Tests UI components in isolation (e.g. React Testing Library, Flutter widget tests)
Steps (PROPOSED): Render each component alone. | Test each state.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each state has a test.

Purpose: Records defects with steps, device or browser info, logs, severity (in kanban.md; issue tracker if one is set up)
Steps (PROPOSED): Record steps, device or browser, logs, and severity. | Add a BUG item to kanban.md through A1.
Verification (PROPOSED): The steps reproduce the defect.

Purpose: Maps each acceptance criterion to test cases; flags criteria with no test
Steps (PROPOSED): Map each acceptance criterion to test IDs. | Flag criteria with no test.
Verification (PROPOSED): Zero unmapped criteria remain unflagged.

Purpose: Writes test run report: passed, failed, skipped, linked defects
Steps (PROPOSED): Collect pass, fail, and skip counts. | List linked defects.
Verification (PROPOSED): Totals match the test runner output.

Purpose: Prepares quality summary; a named human gives GO / NO-GO
Steps (PROPOSED): Prepare the summary: results, coverage, defects. | Request GO or NO-GO from the named approver.
Verification (PROPOSED): The agent does not record GO or NO-GO.

Purpose: Generates clearly labeled synthetic mock data; never uses real personal data
Steps (PROPOSED): Generate data that matches the BFF spec. | Label it as synthetic.
Verification (PROPOSED): No real personal data is used. The label is present.

Purpose: Writes GitHub Actions workflows for lint, test, and build on each PR
Steps (PROPOSED): Write a workflow for lint, test, and build on each PR. | Run it on a test PR.
Verification (PROPOSED): The workflow runs green on the test PR.

Purpose: Configures CI/CD builds and deploys: Fastlane, EAS Build, or Flutter pipelines (mobile); hosting pipelines (web) (includes build config)
Steps (PROPOSED): Configure the build step. | Configure the deploy step with secrets from the vault or GitHub secrets.
Verification (PROPOSED): A dry-run build passes.

Purpose: Applies semantic versioning and generates release notes from merged PRs (includes change summary)
Steps (PROPOSED): Apply semantic versioning from merged PRs. | Generate release notes.
Verification (PROPOSED): The version bump matches the change types.

Purpose: Checks tests green, store metadata ready, privacy labels current, rollback plan set (includes release readiness)
Steps (PROPOSED): Check: tests green, store metadata, privacy labels, rollback plan. | Mark each item with evidence.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every item has evidence.

Purpose: Checks logic, readability, and adherence to team conventions
Steps (PROPOSED): Read the diff against team conventions. | Write comments with severity.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each comment cites a line.

Purpose: Flags API keys, tokens, or keystore data in code, config, or logs
Steps (PROPOSED): Run the scanner on the diff, config, and logs. | List hits.
Verification (PROPOSED): Scanner output is attached to the review.

Purpose: Confirms PR checklist items (tests, docs, screenshots)
Steps (PROPOSED): Compare the PR checklist to the team checklist. | Mark each missing item.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every item is marked present or missing.

Purpose: Outputs findings as blocker / major / minor / nit (includes review report)
Steps (PROPOSED): Group findings as blocker, major, minor, or nit. | Write the summary.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every finding has a severity.

Purpose: Sends findings to developer and re-reviews fixes; stops at a loop limit set in config and escalates to a human
Steps (PROPOSED): Send findings to the developer. | Re-review the fix. | Stop at the loop limit and escalate to a human.
Verification (PROPOSED): Loop count is recorded against the limit. The limit is TBD (R6).

Purpose: Moves items between columns in kanban.md when exit criteria are verified; human-gated moves wait for a recorded approver
Steps (PROPOSED): Receive a status event from an agent. | Check the exit criteria for the column. | Move the item, add a History row, and commit.
Verification (PROPOSED): A History row exists for every move.

Purpose: Confirms each item appears once, in one column, with a History row for every move
Steps (PROPOSED): Check each item appears once. | Check each move has a History row.
Verification (PROPOSED): The report shows zero violations.

Purpose: Verifies exit criteria before moving an item to the next column
Steps (PROPOSED): Read the exit criteria for the column. | Check the evidence for each criterion.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each criterion is recorded as pass or fail.

Purpose: Decides which agent handles a story, bug, or task next
Steps (PROPOSED): Read the item type. | Name the next agent from the agent table.
Verification (PROPOSED): The routing matches the agent table.

Purpose: Blocks a column move until the verification checklist passes and any required human approval is recorded
Steps (PROPOSED): Check the verification checklist. | Allow or block the move.
Verification (PROPOSED): Every blocked move shows its reason.

Purpose: Collects open questions and decision requests from all agents; flags those that block progress
Steps (PROPOSED): Collect open questions from all agents. | Flag those that block progress.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each question has an owner.

Purpose: Every output item cites its source (input ID, Figma node ID, screenshot region, doc section, file and line); untraceable items are flagged
Steps (PROPOSED): Check each output item has a source ID. | Flag items with no source.
Verification (PROPOSED): Zero items are left without a source or a flag.

Purpose: When the source is silent, record the question with options; no default is chosen silently
Steps (PROPOSED): Record each gap with its options. | Do not choose a default.
Verification (PROPOSED): Each entry has at least two options or says TBD.

Purpose: Presents options with trade-offs and waits; a decision is recorded only with a named approver and date
Steps (PROPOSED): List options with trade-offs. | Wait for a named approver.
Verification (PROPOSED): The decision is recorded with a name and a date.

Purpose: Fresh-context pass checks an output against its input and marks each item pass / fail before handoff
Steps (PROPOSED): A fresh-context pass compares the output with its input. | Mark pass or fail per item.
Verification (PROPOSED): Pass or fail is recorded before handoff.

Purpose: Templates for stories, ADRs, test plans, release notes
Steps (PROPOSED): Use the template. | Fill fields from sources only; TBD for gaps.
Verification (PROPOSED): No field lacks a source or TBD.

Purpose: Branches, pull requests, CI status (GitHub: code, PRs, CI only)
Steps (PROPOSED): Create branches, commits, and PRs on GitHub. | Read CI status.
Verification (PROPOSED): CI status is recorded. Only A1 commits kanban.md.
